Back: A high-level programming language focused on readability, with a large standard library and interactive shell support.

Front: What does the interactive shell (REPL) allow you to do? (Ch1)
Back: Run Python instructions one at a time and immediately see results (Read-Evaluate-Print-Loop).

Back: Displays the value/expression inside the parentheses (without showing quotes for strings)

Back: Always a string (even if user types numbers)

List the six comparison operators (Ch2)
Does 42 == 42.0 evaluate to True or False? Why? (Ch2)
Back: True — Python considers integer and equivalent float equal

Front: Which Boolean operator returns True only if both sides are True? (Ch2)
Truth table summary for 'and' (Ch2)
Back: True and True → True; anything else → False

Front: Which operator returns True if at least one side is True? (Ch2)
What does the not operator do? (Ch2)
Back: Inverts the Boolean: not True → False; not False → True

Front: Order of Boolean operator precedence? (Ch2)
What must come after if/elif/while/for before the block? (Ch2)
How does Python determine where a code block starts and ends? (Ch2)
Back: Indentation level (increase starts block, decrease/return to previous ends it)

Front: What happens in an if statement if the condition is False? (Ch2)
Back: The if block is skipped entirely

Front: Syntax of a basic if-else (Ch2)
What is an elif clause used for? (Ch2)
Back: Alternative condition — checked only if previous if/elif were False

Front: Only one of which clauses can exist in a chain: if, elif, else? (Ch2)
Back: else (optional); if is required once; elif zero or more

Front: What do break and continue do inside loops? (Ch2)
Back: break → exit loop completely; continue → skip rest of current iteration, go to next
